en.headline: Disgusting Food Museum continues at Kai Tak through late November
en.dek: The Swedish exhibition at AIRSIDE’s GATE33 Gallery displays more than 80 unusual foods from 35 countries and includes a tasting bar for visitors who want to try them.
body: Sweden’s Disgusting Food Museum remains open at GATE33 Gallery on the third floor of AIRSIDE in Kai Tak until 26 November.

The exhibition presents more than 80 foods from 35 countries that are considered unusual or polarising in some places. Items on display include fermented shark, surströmming and other delicacies that have drawn large crowds in previous cities.

For the Hong Kong edition, the organisers worked with a local perfumer to recreate certain food aromas. Visitors receive a specially designed bag on entry. A tasting bar allows ticket holders to sample selected items under staff guidance.
Opening hours are noon to 8 pm from Monday to Thursday, and 11 am to 9 pm on Fridays, weekends and public holidays. Tickets are available through major local platforms.

zh.headline: 嘔心食物博物館啟德展期至11月底
zh.dek: 瑞典展覽在啟德AIRSIDE GATE33藝文館展出超過80款來自35個國家的奇特食物，並設試食吧供參觀者挑戰。
body: 瑞典的嘔心食物博物館目前仍在啟德AIRSIDE三樓GATE33藝文館展出，展期至11月26日。
展覽展出超過80款來自35個國家、在部分地方被視為奇特或具爭議的食物，包括發酵鯊魚、鹽醃鯤魚等，過往在其他城市已吸引大量參觀者。
香港站特別與本地調香師合作，重現部分食物的氣味。入場者會獲派特製袋子。試食吧讓持票人士在工作人員指導下品嘗選定項目。
開放時間為星期一至四中午12時至晚上8時，星期五、周末及公眾假期則為上午11時至晚上9時。門票可透過主要本地平台購買。
